ac_verdicts.description: DLQ-depth hook fires exactly once on crossing, does not re-fire while above
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: evaluate_trigger/7 at line ~282: ARMED + above threshold → fire and disarm (is_armed := false). FIRED + still above → update sample only, no re-fire. Confirmed by test asserting 3 evaluation cycles fire exactly once.

ac_verdicts.description: Re-arms after falling below threshold; fires a second time on re-crossing
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: evaluate_trigger/7: FIRED + back below threshold → re-arm (is_armed := true). Second crossing fires again.

ac_verdicts.description: Two stuck instances produce two separate deliveries (per-instance trigger_key)
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: evaluate_stuck_instance/4: trigger_key = "instance_error_stuck:#{inst.instance_id}". Each instance gets its own state row.

ac_verdicts.description: Instance stuck below threshold produces no alert; at threshold fires
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: evaluate_stuck_instance/4: effective_threshold = max(threshold_minutes - 1, 0). For threshold=10, effective_threshold=9. stuck_minutes=5 → no fire. stuck_minutes=10 → 10 > 9 → fires.

ac_verdicts.description: Scheduler-lag hook fires via real Poller tick with measurable lag
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: maybe_run_alert_detection/3 at line 201 wires Alerts.build_context_and_detect/3 into the existing tick. Test measures real wall-clock elapsed time and passes it as observed_lag_ms.

ac_verdicts.description: Paused webhook subscription fires exactly one delivery
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: evaluate_paused_subscription/3: trigger_key = "webhook_subscription_paused:#{sub.subscription_id}". Edge-triggered: fires once per ARMED→FIRED crossing.

ac_verdicts.description: POST body for stuck-instance contains instance_id, error_reason, stuck_duration_minutes
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: evaluate_stuck_instance/4 builds payload with instance_id, error_reason, stuck_duration_minutes, fired_at, trigger=instance_error_stuck.

ac_verdicts.description: Failed delivery retries up to max_attempts; exhaustion logs error via REQ-193; NO dlq_entries row
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: fire_hooks/4 → deliver_with_retry/5 → on exhaustion: Logger.error 'alert delivery exhausted'. No Dlq.enqueue/1 call anywhere in alerts.ex (grep confirmed). Moduledoc line 21: 'DLQ landing | **Never** | Yes'.

ac_verdicts.description: auth_secret_ref resolved via REQ-190's Secrets.resolve/2 at delivery time
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: resolve_auth_header/1 at line 517-526: pattern-matches on non-nil ref, calls Secrets.resolve/2. No credential stored inline in AlertHookConfig struct (auth_secret_ref is only the reference string). State tables have no credential columns.

ac_verdicts.description: Both state tables per-tenant, placement stated with reasoning in migration
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: Migration header (lines 18-27): 'PLACEMENT DECISION (PER-TENANT, not global): R-Co places these tables in public schema... Letflow's monitored subjects are structurally different: dlq_entries is per-tenant (Decision B), instance_projections is per-tenant, and webhook_subscriptions is per-tenant.' Both migrations use `if prefix() do` guard and are registered in TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex lines 469, 471).

ac_verdicts.description: No application.ex change; no new periodic child added
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: Test is a source assertion: refute function_exported?(Alerts, :start_link, 1) and refute function_exported?(Alerts, :child_spec, 1). Detection runs via maybe_run_alert_detection/3 inside handle_info(:tick) in poller.ex — the existing supervised GenServer, not a new child. git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/application.ex shows no Alerts reference.

ac_verdicts.description: Moduledoc documents distinction from REQ-181/183 webhook subscriptions
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: Moduledoc lines 9-21 contain the comparison table: '| Property | Alerting hooks (REQ-201) | Webhook subscriptions (REQ-181/183) |' with all six differentiating rows. Test is a source assertion confirming text presence.

ac_verdicts.description: No route or controller file added or modified
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: Test is a source assertion: git diff main...HEAD --stat confirms no lib/letflow/routers/ or lib/letflow/api/ file in the diff. Moduledoc lines 32-37 state 'No route or controller' and 'no Plug module is added or modified'.

ac_verdicts.description: mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test pass; Alerts.run_detection/2 exported; Dlq.count_entries/1 exported
ac_verdicts.implementation_detail: Fix at commit 005e9a8f: Code.ensure_loaded!(Alerts) before function_exported? (line 539). This is the fix TEST-RUNNER applied to address the seed-dependent failure. Independently confirmed: targeted suite 17/17 pass; full suite shows no alerts_test failure; compile exit 0.

notes.full_suite_difference_from_test_runner: TEST-RUNNER's full run hit alerts_test.exs:538 as failure #3; my independent run hit executor_test.exs:224 as failure #3. Both failure sets contain exactly 3 pre-existing failures not in the REQ-201 diff. The difference is ExUnit random seed ordering — executor_test.exs:224 is a wall-clock timeout (timing-sensitive) that did not trigger on TEST-RUNNER's run. executor_test.exs has zero lines changed by this branch (confirmed by git diff main...HEAD).
notes.three_pre_existing_failures_confirmed: All 3 failures in my run: (1) executor_test.exs:224 — wallclock timeout, not in branch diff; (2) sandbox_test.exs — System.cmd(grep) on Windows; (3) host_api_test.exs — System.cmd(grep) on Windows. Zero REQ-201 failures.
